extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, appellate judges, patent prosecutors, and counsel involved in claim construction and indefiniteness disputes
extracted.subtask_description: Appellate court guidance on construing patent claim terms (here, 'Downloadable'), the effect of incorporation-by-reference within a patent family, and the legal standard for indefiniteness and summary judgment on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims construed in light of the specification (Phillips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be read in light of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification provides context for claim terms; this principle includes any patents incorporated by reference. See Phillips v. AWH Corp., 415 F.3d 1303, 1315 (Fed. Cir. 2005) (en banc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of incorporation by reference (X2Y/Ultradent/MPEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents incorporated by reference are effectively part of the host patents as if they were explicitly contained therein; incorporation renders the entire contents of that patent's disclosure a part of the host patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporated material becomes part of the host patent's disclosure and can inform claim construction. See X2Y Attenuators, LLC v. U.S. Int'l Trade Comm'n, 757 F.3d 1358, 1362–63; Ultradent Prods., Inc. v. Life-Like Cosmetics, Inc., 127 F.3d 1065, 1069; MPEP § 608.01(p) (6th ed. 1996).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation does not convert invention of host patent (Modine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference does not convert the invention of the incorporated patent into the invention of the host patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although incorporated disclosure is part of the host, the host patent's own disclosure controls the scope of its invention. Do not assume that incorporation imports the incorporated patent's claimed invention wholesale. See Modine Mfg. Co. v. U.S. Int'l Trade Comm'n, 75 F.3d 1545, 1553.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related-patent disclosures can inform but cannot automatically import disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures of related patents may inform the construction of claim terms common across patents, but it is erroneous to assume that the scope of the invention is the same such that disclaimers of scope necessarily apply across patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When family patents have differing definitions, assess whether those definitions conflict or can coexist; do not mechanically apply the narrowest family definition to the host patent. (Citing X2Y Attenuators and concurring observations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether material has been incorporated by reference is a question of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining whether material has been incorporated by reference into a host document is a legal question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply legal analysis to incorporation-by-reference; factual underpinnings may be reviewed, but incorporation itself is treated as law. See Advanced Display Sys., Inc. v. Kent State Univ., 212 F.3d 1272, 1283.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefiniteness standard under 35 U.S.C. § 112 (Nautilus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is invalid for indefiniteness if its language, when read in light of the specification and prosecution history, fails to inform skilled artisans about the scope of the invention with reasonable certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 'reasonable certainty' Nautilus standard to evaluate whether claim language provides adequate notice of scope to a person of ordinary skill in the art. See Nautilus, Inc. v. Biosig Instruments, Inc., 572 U.S. 898, 909–11 (2014). Indefiniteness determinations are reviewed de novo on appeal (Ethicon Endo-Surgery v. Covidien).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review for claim construction and underlying facts (Teva)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit reviews claim construction de novo and reviews the district court's underlying factual determinations for clear error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When factual issues underlie claim construction, defer to district court's factual findings unless clearly erroneous; otherwise, claim construction legal questions are reviewed de novo. See Teva Pharms. USA, Inc. v. Sandoz, Inc., 574 U.S. 318, 325–26 (2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary judgment standard (regional circuit; here Ninth Circuit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary judgment is proper when, drawing all justifiable inferences in the non-movant’s favor, there is no genuine dispute as to any material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the applicable regional circuit standard for summary judgment (Ninth Circuit in this case). See Fed. R. Civ. P. 56(a); Anderson v. Liberty Lobby, Inc., 477 U.S. 242, 255 (1986); Azko Nobel Coatings, Inc. v. Dow Chem. Co., 811 F.3d 1334, 1338–39 (Fed. Cir. 2016) (applying regional standard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciling differing definitions within a patent family
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent family contains differing definitions of a term, determine whether the definitions are competing or whether they can exist in harmony; do not necessarily limit a host patent to the most restrictive family definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier family member defines a term more restrictively (e.g., 'small' Downloadable focused on applets) but a later patent omits that restriction and includes broader examples, the later patent's broader definition may control for that patent. Do not mechanically import a deleted limiting term from a grandparent application into parent/child patents (see Modine). The court applied this to conclude 'Downloadable' need not include 'small' where later patents expanded examples to ActiveX, scripts, Visual Basic, trojans, compressed files, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specification examples to inform claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples listed in the specification (e.g., Java applets, ActiveX controls, JavaScript scripts, Visual Basic scripts, Trojan horses, compressed files) can expand a term's meaning and support a broader construction of a claim term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a specification provides multiple examples beyond a sole example in an earlier incorporated patent, those examples can indicate the patentee intended broader coverage. The court relied on examples in the '844, '780, '086, '621, and '755 patents to support a construction of 'Downloadable' without a 'small' size limitation.
